connection_flow.description: Trace from MCP client connection to tool execution

steps.action: Sends HTTP POST to /mcp with Authorization Bearer token (runtime credential)
steps.details: The runtime credential is a secret that cryptographically identifies the client as either 'claude' or 'hermes'

steps.action: OPTIONS preflight allowed, then authMiddleware applied
steps.details: Lines 464-539: The endpoint first allows OPTIONS, then applies authMiddleware before any other processing

steps.action: Extracts Authorization header and validates token
steps.details: In local-single-user mode, validates runtime credentials via validateRuntimeCredential(). In other modes, validates session tokens. If valid token in local mode, creates AuthContext with runtime from credential.
Lines 488-496: Verifies the authenticated session owns the active runtime connection. In bootstrap mode (local-founder), this check is bypassed.
Lines 502-511: Acquires an execution permit via BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. Verifies session exists, matches active runtime, lease is valid. Inserts execution record.

steps.action: Creates McpServer and handles request via StreamableHTTPServerTransport
steps.details: Lines 516-524: Creates new McpServer per request, registers tools with authContext callback, handles the request. Tools receive authContext that includes the runtime from credential validation.
mcp/tools.ts: createToolHandler validates ctx exists and calls requireAuthenticated. Tools check ctx.owner_type, ctx.runtime for authorization. Runtime is set from credential, not chosen by caller.

identified_issues.title: Bootstrap session identity is hardcoded to 'claude' regardless of connecting agent
identified_issues.description: In local-single-user mode, when no valid runtime credential is provided, the authMiddleware creates an AuthContext with runtime='claude' hardcoded. This means if a Hermes client connects via bootstrap, it will be identified as Claude.
identified_issues.impact: A Hermes client connecting via local bootstrap would be incorrectly identified as Claude. This could lead to wrong runtime identity being used for operations. The execution guard may allow tools to execute under wrong runtime context.

identified_issues.title: Execution guard skips runtime identity verification for bootstrap sessions
identified_issues.description: In acquireExecutionPermit(), for bootstrap sessions (isBootstrapSession=true), the code does NOT verify that the authenticated runtime matches the active session's runtime. It only checks if session_id matches.
identified_issues.impact: If the active runtime is 'hermes' but bootstrap is used, the execution guard will allow tools to execute. The runtime from bootstrap (hardcoded 'claude') may not match the active session's runtime.
identified_issues.trace: server.ts line 502 creates guard -> runtime-execution-guard.ts line 50-221 -> isBootstrapSession skips lines 121-171 that verify runtime matches

identified_issues.title: ESM import path may fail silently during database operations
identified_issues.description: Uses require() for runtime credentials and database imports at runtime rather than top-level imports. If the module fails to load, the error is caught and silently falls through to bootstrap mode.
identified_issues.impact: A module load failure could cause the system to fall back to bootstrap authentication unexpectedly, potentially bypassing credential validation. The catch block at line 95-98 catches all errors without logging, making debugging difficult.

identified_issues.title: Local-mode auto-authentication overrides credentials when DATABASE not available
identified_issues.description: When the database is not available (e.g., during startup or if databaseInstance is null), the code falls through to bootstrap mode even if a valid token was provided.
identified_issues.impact: During database downtime or initialization, valid runtime credentials would be silently ignored and the request would be auto-authenticated as bootstrap-founder with hardcoded 'claude' runtime.

identified_issues.title: MCP endpoint does not validate runtime ownership before creating execution guard
identified_issues.description: The server.ts /mcp endpoint checks runtime ownership (line 489) but then creates a fresh execution guard that re-checks ownership. If ownership check passes, the execution guard creates a new permit. There's potential for race condition between the two checks.
identified_issues.impact: The two-phase check could theoretically allow a race condition. If the active session changes between the ownership check and permit acquisition, the system may behave unexpectedly. However, the execution guard uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE so this is partially mitigated.

identified_issues.title: Session ID 'local-founder' is a magic string used in multiple places
identified_issues.description: The string 'local-founder' is hardcoded in three different locations to identify bootstrap sessions. Changes in one place could cause inconsistencies.

identified_issues.title: Bootstrap session creation may fail UNIQUE constraint if same session_id already connected
identified_issues.description: The bootstrap logic at line 77 clears expired sessions, and line 85-88 disconnects existing active session, but line 95-108 then attempts to upsert. If the same session_id='local-founder' is trying to connect while another is already connected, there could be a race.
identified_issues.mitigation: SQLite's upsert with ON CONFLICT handles this, but the logic is complex and relies on correct ordering of operations within the transaction.

recommendations.title: Fix bootstrap session runtime to accept client-provided runtime
recommendations.recommendation: In local-single-user mode, when no valid credential token is provided, accept a runtime parameter from the request body or header instead of hardcoding 'claude'. Modify authentication.ts to extract runtime from request body.
recommendations.code_change: authentication.ts:102-118 - accept runtime from request body when falling back to bootstrap
implementation: 1. Accept optional 'runtime' field in request body for bootstrap mode
2. Validate runtime is 'claude' or 'hermes'
3. Use provided runtime in AuthContext instead of hardcoded 'claude'
4. Update tests to verify Hermes can bootstrap

recommendations.title: Verify runtime identity in bootstrap session acquisition
recommendations.recommendation: Add runtime verification to bootstrap session handling in runtime-execution-guard.ts. Even for bootstrap, ensure the runtime matches what was authenticated.
recommendations.code_change: runtime-execution-guard.ts:72-109 - add runtime check for bootstrap sessions
implementation: 1. Extract runtime from authContext for bootstrap
2. Before upserting, check if active session runtime matches
3. If mismatch, disconnect old session and create new (or reject based on config)
4. Or: Require runtime credential even in local mode for bootstrap

recommendations.title: Add logging and error handling for dynamic imports
recommendations.recommendation: Replace silent catch blocks with proper error logging. The current code silently falls through to bootstrap on any error, which could mask real problems.
implementation: 1. Add console.error or logger.error in catch block
2. Include error message in the log
3. Consider returning 500 error if credential validation fails due to system error
4. Add context about what operation was attempted

recommendations.title: Reject requests with invalid credentials during database unavailability
recommendations.recommendation: During database downtime, reject requests with invalid credentials rather than falling back to bootstrap. Bootstrap should only be a fallback for requests without credentials.
recommendations.code_change: authentication.ts:57-100 - separate credential validation path from bootstrap fallback
implementation: 1. If token is provided but database unavailable, return 503 or 401
2. Only use bootstrap for requests with no Authorization header
3. Add health check endpoint to detect database availability

recommendations.title: Consolidate ownership checking into single atomic operation
recommendations.recommendation: Consider removing the pre-check in server.ts and rely solely on execution guard's atomic transaction. This simplifies the flow and eliminates potential race windows.
recommendations.code_change: server.ts:478-539 - remove redundant ownership check, rely on execution guard
implementation: 1. Remove createRuntimeOwnershipGuard check from server.ts /mcp endpoint
2. Move all ownership logic into acquireExecutionPermit()
3. Return appropriate error codes from permit acquisition
4. Simplify server.ts to just call execution guard

recommendations.title: Define constant for bootstrap session ID
recommendations.recommendation: Create a shared constant for 'local-founder' session_id to prevent typos and ease maintenance.
recommendations.code_change: runtime-types.ts or auth/index.ts - add BOOTSTRAP_SESSION_ID constant
implementation: 1. Define BOOTSTRAP_SESSION_ID = 'local-founder' in runtime-types.ts or auth/index.ts
2. Update all three locations to use the constant
3. Export for use in other modules if needed

critical_concerns: Bootstrap session in local mode hardcodes runtime='claude' regardless of connecting client identity
Execution guard skips runtime identity verification for bootstrap sessions
Credential validation falls through to bootstrap on any error, including when valid token is provided but database unavailable
security_positive_findings: Credential-based auth correctly determines runtime from stored credential, not from caller
TOCTOU protection via BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions in execution guard
30-second execution permit timeout prevents stale executions
5-minute heartbeat renewal interval for session management
UNIQUE constraint on runtime_sessions(session_id) prevents session hijacking
Partial unique index on connection_status='connected' enforces single active runtime

test_coverage_details: Credential generation for both claude and hermes
Token validation with various error conditions (missing, invalid, expired, revoked, oversized)
Tests verify that claude credential identifies as claude, hermes as hermes (identity cannot be spoofed)
